{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Build

on:
  push:
    branches: [ master ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ master ]
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  test:
    strategy:
      matrix:
        go-version: [1.16.x, 1.17.x, 1.18.x, 1.19.x, 1.20.x, 1.21.x, 1.22.x, 1.23.x, 1.24.x, 1.25.x, 1.26.x, tip]
        full-tests: [false]
        include:
          - go-version: 1.27.x
            full-tests: true

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Setup go
        run: |
          curl -sL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/maxatome/install-go/v3.8/install-go.pl |
              perl - ${{ matrix.go-version }} $HOME/go

      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v2

      - name: Cache Go modules
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/go/pkg/mod
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-go-${{ hashFiles('go.mod', 'go.sum') }}

      - name: Miscellaneous checks
        if: matrix.full-tests
        run: |
          ./tools/gen_funcs.pl
          git diff --exit-code
          if fgrep 'interface{}' $(find . -name '*.go' -not -name any.go -not -name any_test.go); then
              echo '*** At least one interface{} occurrence found. Use any instead.'
              false
          fi

      - name: Linting
        if: matrix.full-tests
        run: |
          curl -sL https://golangci-lint.run/install.sh |
              sh -s -- -b $HOME/go/bin v2.13.0
          $HOME/go/bin/golangci-lint run

      - name: Testing
        continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.go-version == 'tip' }}
        run: |
          go version
          go env
          if [ -z "$(go env GOPROXY)" ]; then
              echo "Fix empty GOPROXY"
              export GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org,direct
          fi
          if [ ${{ matrix.full-tests }} = true ]; then
              cover_flags="-coverpkg=./... -covermode=atomic -test.gocoverdir=$(pwd)/cov/"
              GO_TEST_BASE_FLAGS="$cover_flags"base
              GO_TEST_SAFE_FLAGS="$cover_flags"safe
              GO_TEST_RACE_FLAGS="$cover_flags"race
              GO_TEST_RACE_SAFE_FLAGS="$cover_flags"race-safe
              GO_TEST_RACE_CGO_FLAGS="$cover_flags"cgo
              mkdir -p cov/base cov/safe cov/race cov/race-safe cov/cgo
          fi

          export GORACE="halt_on_error=1"
          echo "BASE ==========================================="
          go test                  ./... $GO_TEST_BASE_FLAGS
          echo "SAFE =============================================="
          go test       -tags safe ./... $GO_TEST_SAFE_FLAGS
          echo "RACE =============================================="
          go test -race            ./... $GO_TEST_RACE_FLAGS
          echo "RACE + SAFE ======================================="
          go test -race -tags safe ./... $GO_TEST_RACE_SAFE_FLAGS
          echo "RACE + CGO (internal/spew only) ==================="
          CGO_ENABLED=1 \
              go test -race -tags testcgo ./internal/spew $GO_TEST_RACE_CGO_FLAGS

      - name: Reporting
        if: matrix.full-tests
        env:
          COVERALLS_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          dirs=
          for d in cov/*; do
              [ -d $d ] && dirs="${dirs:+"$dirs,"}$d"
          done
          go tool covdata textfmt -i="$dirs" -o /dev/fd/1 |
              egrep -v '^github\.com/maxatome/go-testdeep/internal/(json/parser\.go:|test/)' > coverage.out
          go install github.com/mattn/goveralls@v0.0.12
          goveralls -coverprofile=coverage.out -service=github
",
  "rationale": "The workflow downloads Go modules during the test step but does not cache them. Adding a cache step for ~/go/pkg/mod keyed by go.mod and go.sum is a low-risk optimization supported by literature (P-LIT-GHA-CACHE) and a measured experiment showing ~6% elapsed time reduction. The repository has go.mod and go.sum, satisfying the cache key requirements. The cache step is placed after checkout and before any Go commands that fetch dependencies, preserving all existing test coverage and behavior.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE", "experiment:batch-interactive-three--f6d2974a5cef7cc9"]
}

First, analyze the workflow:
- It's a Go project with a matrix of Go versions (1.16.x to 1.26.x and tip) and a special case for 1.27.x with full-tests.
- The job runs on ubuntu-latest.
- Steps: Setup go (using a custom script), Checkout code, Miscellaneous checks (only for full-tests), Linting (only for full-tests), Testing (with various flags and coverage), Reporting (only for full-tests).

Potential optimizations from evidence:
1. Caching Go modules (P-LIT-GHA-CACHE) - evidence shows adding actions/cache for ~/go/pkg/mod with key based on go.mod and go.sum.
2. Custom timeout (P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT) - evidence shows adding timeout-minutes to jobs.
3. Fail-fast for matrix (P-LIT-FAIL-FAST) - evidence shows setting strategy.fail-fast: true.

For caching Go modules:
- The workflow downloads Go modules in the testing step (go test ...). It does not have an explicit "go mod download" step, but go test will download dependencies.
- The evidence example (experiment:batch-interactive-three--f6d2974a5cef7cc9) shows adding a cache step before "Install dependencies" (which is go mod download). In our workflow, there is no explicit go mod download step, but we can add a cache step before the testing step to cache ~/go/pkg/mod.
- The repository has go.mod and go.sum (go.sum is empty in the provided context, but it exists). The cache key can be based on hashFiles('go.mod', 'go.sum').
- This seems applicable and safe.

For custom timeout:
- The workflow currently has no timeout. The job runs a matrix of Go versions and multiple test suites. It might benefit from a timeout to prevent runaway jobs.
- Evidence shows adding timeout-minutes: 5 to jobs. However, we need to choose an appropriate timeout. The evidence examples used 5 minutes. Our job might take longer because it runs many tests. We need to be careful not to set too low a timeout that would cause false failures.
- The pattern P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT requires "Representative successful-duration history exists". We have some CI history (5 runs) but they are all successful. Since we don't have per-job history, it's risky. However, the pattern is supported by evidence. We could propose a timeout of 10 minutes.

That suggests that failures in tip are allowed. Also, the matrix includes many versions; we might want to see all results. The pattern P-LIT-FAIL-FAST has contraindications: "Every matrix outcome is required" and "Full failure diagnostics are required". In this workflow, it might be that they want to test all Go versions. The `continue-on-error` for tip indicates they don't want to fail the whole build for tip. But for other versions, they might want to see all failures. The pattern's preconditions: "Matrix failure makes remaining results dispensable under an explicit study policy". We don't know the policy. The evidence examples are synthetic. It might be applicable, but we need to be cautious.

The cache step should be placed after checkout and before the testing step (or before any step that downloads modules). In the workflow, the first step that downloads modules is the Testing step (go test). There's also a step for linting that installs golangci-lint, but that's a binary, not Go modules. The evidence uses key: `${{ runner.os }}-go-${{ hashFiles('go.mod', 'go.sum') }}`. That does not include Go version. However, the Go module cache is version-agnostic? Actually, the module cache is shared across Go versions. But the Go version might affect which modules are downloaded? Usually not. It's safe to use the same cache key for all matrix jobs. However, if we want to be safe, we could include the Go version in the key. But the evidence doesn't. We'll follow the evidence.

We'll add a step:
      - name: Cache Go modules
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/go/pkg/mod
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-go-${{ hashFiles('go.mod', 'go.sum') }}

We need to place it after checkout and before the Testing step. Also, note that the workflow has conditional steps for full-tests. The cache step should run for all matrix jobs (since all run go test). So we can put it right after checkout.

Now, we must produce the updated workflow YAML.

We'll also consider adding a custom timeout. But we need to decide on a value. The workflow runs multiple test suites. The longest run in history is about 4 minutes. But that's the whole workflow (all matrix jobs). The matrix jobs run in parallel, so each job might take up to 4 minutes. To be safe, we could set timeout-minutes: 10. However, the evidence for custom timeout shows 5 minutes. But that's for other projects. We don't have strong evidence for this specific workflow. The pattern requires "Representative successful-duration history exists". We have 5 successful runs, but we don't have per-job durations. It's risky. We might skip this optimization.

Since the workflow tests many Go versions, they might want to know which versions fail. So fail-fast might not be appropriate.

Thus, the best supported optimization is caching Go modules.

We'll produce the updated workflow with the cache step added.

We'll use evidence_ids from the caching experiment: "experiment:batch-interactive-three--f6d2974a5cef7cc9". Also the pattern P-LIT-GHA-CACHE is supported by literature. We can include both? The instruction says "Use only supported evidence IDs; APPLY requires at least one." We'll include the experiment ID and the pattern ID? The evidence IDs are the document_ids from the evidence list. The evidence list includes experiment records and pattern catalogue. The pattern catalogue entries have document_id like "pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE". We can use those. The instruction says "Use only supported evidence IDs". We'll include the experiment ID and the pattern ID.

But note: the evidence list provided includes both experiment examples and pattern catalogue. The pattern catalogue is also evidence. We'll include the pattern ID "pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE" and the experiment ID "experiment:batch-interactive-three--f6d2974a5cef7cc9".
